visibility.description: Who sees each Note on the timelines.

Announce.description: `[announce]`: how a run holds and keeps an announcement.

latest_attempts.description:
How often a run writes what a project last announced again when
another write lands between its read and its write; 3 where absent.

lease.description:
How long a run holds an announcement past its last write before
another may finish it; "20m" where absent, longer than the longest a
host lets one run go on, a Lambda's 15 minutes.

App.description: An app of the HTTP API (ADR-0007).

routes.description:
The routes it announces to, each naming the app among its sources;
every such route where it names none.

tokens.description:
The SHA-256 of each of the app's tokens, written `sha256:` and 64
lowercase hex digits, as `herald token new` prints it. A token is
rotated by adding the new one before the old one is removed.

ArchiveAfter.description:
How long a quiet thread stays open before Discord archives it: one of the
four lengths Discord takes.

oneOf.description: An hour.
A day.
Three days.
A week, the longest Discord keeps a quiet thread open.

Audience.description: Who sees an actor's Notes on the timelines. Followers see every Note.

oneOf.description: Everyone, on the public timelines too.
Everyone who looks, kept off the public timelines.

Colours.description: The colours of an announcement's embed, each where the config sets one.

prerelease.description:
A pre-release's colour; the violet of herald's banner, `#8f88c7`,
where unset.

release.description:
A release's colour; the gold of herald's trumpet, `#e39a26`, where
unset.

Http.description:
`[http]`: how herald's own requests reach the services a config names.
None of it applies to the hosts herald reaches on others' behalf, an
`ActivityPub` actor's key or a follower's inbox (ADR-0007).

body.description:
The most bytes of a response's body herald reads; "32MiB" where
absent, and at most "128MiB". A host reached on others' behalf is
read no further than "32MiB" whatever this says.

ca_file.description:
A PEM file of the certificate authorities herald's own requests trust
beside the Mozilla roots, read beside the config, such as a GitHub
Enterprise Server's private CA.

connect.description: How long a connection may take to open; "10s" where absent.

total.description:
How long a request may take, from sending it to the end of its
answer; "30s" where absent. `HERALD_TIMEOUT_MS` takes its place.

Inbound.description:
`[server.inbound]`: what a signed inbound request may carry and still be
checked. Each bound may be at most four times its default, and doctor
names one set above it.

covered.description:
The most headers one ActivityPub signature may cover; 16 where
absent, at least the 4 it must cover, and at most 64.

replay_window.description:
How far a signed timestamp may lie from now, either way, before the
request is taken for a replay; "5m" where absent, and at most "20m".

signatures.description:
The most signatures a request may carry, each checked in turn; 4
where absent, and at most 16.

domains.description: Domains beside `discord.gg` a gateway session may connect under, such as a proxy's.

guild.description:

key.description:

os.description:

prefix.description:

sender.description: The application service's user, by its localpart.

template.description:

in place of the route's own.

timeline.description:

domains.description:
Domains beside its Slack's own a Socket Mode session may connect
under, such as a proxy's.

name.description:

signing.description:

posted to herald is checked against.

in place of the route's own.

KeyCache.description: Where `herald server` keeps the keys inbound activities are checked with.

oneOf.description: In memory, lost when the server stops.
In the store, kept across restarts and shared by every instance.

Keys.description: `[server.keys]`: the keys inbound activities are checked with.

cache.description: Where they are kept: "memory", the default, or "store".

document.description:
The most of a key's or an actor's document read; "256KiB" where
absent, and at most "1MiB".

most.description:
The most kept in memory, the one used longest ago forgotten first;
1024 where absent.

refresh_after.description:
How long a key is used before its document is read again; 1h where
absent.

reread_after.description:
How long after a key is read an activity that does not hold under it
is refused rather than having it read again; 1m where absent.

Kind.description: What kind of thing an event announces.

`[render]`: how far a template may go as it renders. Each bound may be
at most four times its default, and doctor names one set above it.

fuel.description:
The fuel one render may burn; 100000 where absent, and at most
400000.

output.description: The most it may write; "256KiB" where absent, and at most "1MiB".

recursion.description:
How deep its loops and calls may nest; 16 where absent, and at most
64.

`subscribe` and `unsubscribe` are always the asker's alone.

Route.description:
A route: what it takes, where it announces, and its destination's own
options, as its destination's kind defines them.

Server.description: `[server]`: how `herald server` listens, and what it takes on at once.

accept_pause.description:
How long the server waits after a connection could not be accepted;
"100ms" where absent.

base.description:
The path every endpoint is served under, for a reverse proxy that
serves herald beside other things, as "/herald"; the root where
absent. herald's ActivityPub actors' ids are under it too.

body.description:
The most an inbound request's body may hold; "1MiB" where absent,
and at most "4MiB".

busy_retry.description:
How long a request whose work found no place is asked to wait, in
its `Retry-After`; "30s" where absent.

completions.description:
How many autocompletions a session answers at once; one arriving
while as many are answered is dropped. 4 where absent.

connections.description: How many connections it holds at once; 256 where absent.

deliveries.description:
How many of an announcement's inboxes are delivered to at once, by
every command; 8 where absent.

fetches.description: How many actor documents it reads at once; 4 where absent.

held.description:
How long a connection is held at most, its one request answered;
"90s", or `read` where that is longer, where absent; at least `read`.

inbound.description: What a signed inbound request may carry and still be checked.

jobs.description: How many announcements it works on at once; 8 where absent.

keys.description: The keys inbound activities are checked with.

listen.description:
The address and port it listens on; `--listen` and `HERALD_LISTEN`
take its place. "127.0.0.1:8080" where absent, for a reverse proxy
in front of it.

queue.description:
How many announcements may wait for a place; a webhook arriving while
as many wait is answered 503. As many as `jobs` where absent.

read.description:
How long a connection may take to send a request's headers; "30s"
where absent.

sessions.description: How a session a destination holds waits before it connects again.

silence.description:
How long a session a destination holds hears nothing before it
checks the connection is alive, and then as long again before it
opens another; "30s" where absent.

Sessions.description:
`[server.sessions]`: how a session a destination holds waits before it
connects again, each wait double the last up to the longest.

first_wait.description: The first wait after a session fails to connect; "1s" where absent.

jitter.description:
Whether each wait is between half of it and all of it, so sessions
that failed together do not all connect again at once; true where
absent.

longest_wait.description:
The longest wait between attempts; "1m" where absent, and at least
`first_wait`.

Size.description: A number of bytes: a number and KiB or MiB, as "1MiB".

Via.description: How Discord carries commands to herald.

oneOf.description:
Discord posts each interaction to herald's endpoint, signed with the
application's key: served by `herald server` and by a serverless
driver.

herald holds a connection to Discord's gateway and takes each
interaction from it: served by `herald server`, with no public
endpoint.

Via2.description: How the homeserver carries commands to herald.

oneOf.description:
The homeserver pushes each room event to herald as an application
service, with the registration `herald matrix registration` writes:
served by `herald server` and by a serverless driver.

herald syncs as the bot account and reads each message in the rooms
it has joined: served by `herald server`, with no public endpoint and
nothing for the homeserver's administrator to install.

Via3.description: How Slack carries commands to herald.

oneOf.description:
Slack posts each command and button press to herald's endpoint,
signed with the app's signing secret: served by `herald server` and
by a serverless driver.

herald holds a Socket Mode connection, opened with the app-level
token, and takes each one from it: served by `herald server`, with no
public endpoint.
